scenarios.scope: Strict schema-valid experimental configurations; not the frozen GT denominator. The immutable GT release contains 93 scenarios.

known_limitations: FILE_WRITE is not emitted by the process probe. Successful FILE_OPEN records FileOpen + flags and does not prove contents were read/written. Raw syscall entry/exit pairs retain return values and outcome; failed/pending/unknown operations do not create completed-fact graph edges. File mutation/connect/send events also require completed outcome. EXEC is the PROCESS_EXEC alias.
HTTP/2 is not parsed (only HTTP/1.1 plaintext). HTTP/3/QUIC is structurally unreachable via SSL_read/SSL_write.

Connection-close-delimited responses (no Transfer-Encoding and no Content-Length) are not synthesized: their completion is unknowable, so they pass through raw. Compressed/chunked responses are decoded by PayloadNormalizer (P1); malformed or incomplete messages emit an explicit decode_status diagnostic instead of being silently dropped.
`intent_class` is persisted in lower case and the benchmark scripts count `intent_class='side_effect'`; this spelling is a load-bearing measurement contract and must not be changed.
The `observed`-vs-`asserted` identity split cannot separate N logical agents inside one OS process; the product promises a candidate set with grades, not a unique answer.

Raw SSL events (and their `data_b64`) are captured verbatim. Before any output, `RawSecretRedactor` rewrites the values of Authorization / Proxy-Authorization / Cookie / Set-Cookie / X-Api-Key inside HTTP heads and marks the event with a `redaction` object; the capture itself stays byte-exact. Residual: request/response bodies and arbitrary free text are not redacted, and a header value split across two TLS records evades redaction by design (half-redacting would keep the visible prefix).

stdio payloads are captured verbatim. Before any output, `StdioSecretRedactor` applies the shape-based `export::genai::redact` patterns to the event's `data` string and records a `redaction` object (`captured_data_bytes` / `redacted_data_bytes`); the capture itself is not modified. JSON input is redacted in a JSON-aware mode that replaces values only (object members, JSON embedded as an escaped string, array/numeric values under a sensitive key, header/label text inside a string) so the payload stays valid JSON; non-JSON input uses the header and `key=value` rules. Residual: an opaque credential with no recognizable prefix or key label; a key written with JSON unicode escapes (`\u0070assword`); a credential split across two read(2)/write(2) events (each event is redacted independently, like a header split across TLS records); fd_target / comm / argv are not redacted. Process `full_command` captures argv verbatim and is not redacted.

External-content provenance has a scoped seed: instruction-bearing prompt_injection/role_forgery signals are associated with observed FileWrite/FileOverwrite, matching intent paths and context propagation in graph_builder.rs. Arbitrary file read/stdin bytes do not form a generally enabled directive seed. Capture and payload redaction do not by themselves establish malicious instruction semantics.

Dependency audit scope: `cargo audit` covers every Rust dependency and `npm audit` covers *production* npm dependencies (`--omit=dev`). Dev-only tooling (storybook, vitest, eslint and their transitive tree) still reports advisories; it never reaches the embedded artifact, and is treated as a build-tool trust-boundary risk rather than budgeted. `scripts/audit-budget.json` currently accepts no advisories (both lists empty).

Agent ownership is decided by `comm ∈ AGENT_COMMS` (default `claude`, `claude-code`) or by agent ancestry in the signal graph. An agent that runs under a different `comm` (e.g. OpenClaw's Node gateway runs as `MainThread`) must extend the boundary with `MTAGENTLENS_AGENT_COMMS=name1,name2`; actions outside the boundary are counted as `actions_dropped_no_agent` in the run's `[diagnostics:json]` line instead of being dropped invisibly.

Path normalization is deliberately not one function: `evidence::args` normalizes intent/action keys (strip `./`, collapse `//`), `evidence::argument_matcher` resolves `.`/`..` for argument matching, and `graph_builder` normalizes policy keys (strip `~/` and `./`). Each has a different contract and its own tests; unifying them would change matching semantics.

Two `FilterExpression`/`FilterNode` grammars (SSL: binary And/Or over `data|function|latency_ms`; HTTP: n-ary And/Or over `request|response` targets) and two `json_to_event` timestamp preferences (process emits `timestamp`, tls_capture emits `timestamp_ns`) are intentional per-producer behaviours, not duplicate implementations.

Replay's ablation switches (`skip_identity_resolution`, `skip_attribution`, `skip_ai_pipeline`, `skip_content_boundary_signals`, `enabled_match_levels`, `enabled_action_types`) were never read by the executor; the inert `ReplayConfig` API was removed rather than kept as a no-op, matching the earlier removal of `--disable-signal` and `--persisted-graph-replay`.

Persistence backpressure: the live per-event path uses a bounded channel and drops rows under sustained overload (counted as `lost_persist_count`, reported as DEGRADED at finalize; the first 20 drops log their record kind). `trigger()`/`finalize()` batch paths use a blocking send. An evidence row is written only when its intent and action were successfully queued, so a dropped parent never turns into a FOREIGN KEY cascade.

Agent identity beyond `comm`: `MTAGENTLENS_AGENT_EXE` (substring of the executable path or full command line) extends the boundary when `comm` is uninformative (Node sets it to `MainThread`). `MTAGENTLENS_AGENT_CGROUP` is not supported: cgroup unit names have no kernel-verified source after the unverified procfs PID reads were removed, so it is reported at startup and ignored instead of enabling a boundary that can never match. `MTAGENTLENS_AGENT_COMMS` is also unioned into the process probe's `-c` filter; without that union the eBPF FILTER mode never emits the agent's events.

Measurement isolation is opt-in and applies to the benchmark path: `mtagentlens-benchmark run --clean-profile` isolates settings/MCP/hooks/skills/memory/environment, and `--agent-binary`/`--agent-comm` (or `scripts/wire/run-benign-fpr.sh`) exec a copy of the agent ELF with a distinct inode and a <=15-byte comm so TLS uprobes and the process filter exclude the interactive session. Direct `mtagentlens record -c claude` runs still capture any same-comm process by design; do not use them for FPR/overhead evidence. See docs/evaluation/measurement-isolation.md.

OpenClaw structured tool calls are available out-of-band: `MTAGENTLENS_OPENCLAW_STATE=~/.openclaw MTAGENTLENS_OPENCLAW_AGENTS=main` enables `OpenClawRunner`, which polls `trajectory_runtime_events.tool.call` read-only and emits `OutOfBandAsserted` intents correlated with the gateway's observed actions. The asserted `agent_key` (e.g. `agent:main:main`) is preserved in the event but is not yet a distinct graph AgentId; process attribution uses the gateway PID + comm/exe boundary; cgroup unit names are unavailable.

Previously committed runtime credentials were removed from the current source and reachable Git refs during repository cleanup. Private recovery bundles may retain historical values and stay local. Provider-side revocation is independent of repository cleanup; committed templates and fixtures use synthetic credentials.

Live run (`/api/runs/active`): a `record`/`trace` process serves its own `<log>.responsibility.db` as run id `live`; archived runs are reported as active only when their summary says `state=running`. A run directory's name and `summary.json.run_id` are not the database run UUID: the server resolves alerts/evidence through the DB `runs` table and refuses (409) to mix multiple runs. HTTP/2, HTTP/3/QUIC remain out of scope (NONGOAL-01).

Schema v5 scopes entity keys and foreign keys by run_id, persists outcome and analysis checkpoints. Migration rollback/backup and legacy reads have focused regressions; unknown historical outcome remains unknown.

Production graph/evidence/alerts/snapshots/DB routes live in collector/src/server/web.rs. Multi-run resolution is explicit; exported DB is a consistent, scoped SQLite backup with foreign-key validation and VACUUM. There is no implemented HTTP /diff endpoint.

Replay re-evaluates frozen analysis inputs/config under a matching source fingerprint using the same pure decision kernel; it does not re-execute wire decoding, external models, or kernel collection. Missing checkpoint or fingerprint mismatch rejects authoritative recomputation. GT-free replay has no precision/recall/F1.

Observer reviews are bound to candidate ID, version, and exact evidence. Empty or mismatched scope cannot produce authoritative Unsafe; incomplete review and candidate overflow remain unreviewed. Timeout/body limits constrain external review.

TaintedContextUse requires receiver/crossing alignment, shared observation, observed confidence and lack of direct observed delegation. It is an investigative signal; historical numeric effects are invalid for current code and require new experiments.

No hosted CI/CD is configured (ADR-0014). Offline verification uses scripts/verify.sh; browser/kernel checks and network dependency audits are separate. The full capability/type generator remains unimplemented and is not claimed as a passing gate.

Scientific evidence is reported per frozen experiment in docs/evaluation/CURRENT-EVIDENCE.md and compare/results/. The final FuxiBench cohort contains 93 scenarios (58 attack, 35 benign); its scenario labels were reviewed and revised by three named human annotators. Identity and attribution still require separate run-level references. New source builds do not inherit earlier measurement results. Official baseline claims require the actual tool and protocol.

Capture completeness is unknown until source final stats and clean drain are observed. The harmless Linux 7.0 run recorded 9 process-probe dropped events under host-wide capture; this is reported as degraded, not zero loss.

Event-level alignment between the native launch ledger and collector events is unavailable: they share no verifiable event identifier (ADR-0016). A run binding may claim only that the top-level launched process corresponds to a kernel process via pid/start-time and clock witnesses; timestamp proximity or command-string similarity is not evidence, and identity/root-cause metrics must not be computed from this binding.

Run-level annotation is local tooling: previews blind scenario/run identifiers, the codebook `pilot/1` was finalised on 2026-10-24 (authorisation-envelope procedure, per-category `succeeded` criteria, empty-root rule, adjudication/agreement thresholds, blinding scope) and its consistency rules (monotone attempted>=executed>=succeeded) are enforced server-side; a codebook-version migration tool rebinds frozen bundles without moving evidence bytes; but no real human labels, kappa, or `paper_metrics_available=true` exist. Cgroup unit names remain unknown; raw kernel cgroup IDs are retained but no verified resolver exists.

unbacked_graph_types.reason: The runtime graph builder constructs only Agent/Resource/PolicyBoundary node types; its resource kinds are File/Network/Process/ToolCall/Credential. AgentDelegatesTo and ContextFlowsFrom are now produced for observed cross-agent orchestration. The remaining edge/node types are synonyms or concepts with no builder path; templates do not use them. A contract test (collector/tests/graph_pattern_contract.rs) forbids a template from requiring an undeclared type or kind and forces this list to shrink when a producer lands.
